comment: The conflicts the merge settled and how they are told (docs/synchronisation.md §11.7.3, §13.4; src/shared/sync-conflicts.ts). `settle` holds, for each case of sync-merge-vectors.json (`source: "vectors"`) and of sync-merge-draws.json (`source: "draws"`) that has a conflict, the journal lines (`entries`) and the sentences (`views`: keys of the catalogue and the words to put in them) the Mac gives, with `now` the end of the session and `peer` the other device; the merge is run on the three snapshots of the source and `withheld`, this device being the one the peer is not. It is a file snapshot: src/shared/sync-conflicts.test.ts rewrites it with `pnpm exec vitest run src/shared/sync-conflicts.test.ts -u` and refuses a difference otherwise, and LuciumKit (SyncConflictVectorTests) plays it against the Swift. `journal.retention` gives `[id, settledAt]` pairs and the ids that must be left, newest first; `journal.parse` the text of a file and what is read from it.

settle.name: the same field changed differently: the later mark wins
equal time and counter: the greater device id wins
two values with the same mark (never stamped): the greater canonical text wins
a field removed on one side and changed on the other: the later mark wins
the same id added on both sides: merged field by field from an empty base
deleted on one side, modified on the other: kept, the deletion loses
a folder deleted on one side while a tab moves into it on the other: the folder is kept
an unknown field changed on both sides is a conflict like any other
order: both reorder: the later mark wins and what the other side added goes to the end
first synchronisation (empty base): the union, a conflict is settled by the mark
empty base: a change newer than the tombstone brings the entity back
two values with the same mark: compared by UTF-16 code unit, not by UTF-8 byte (the smiley is below U+FF5E)
a tab put in two different folders: the later mark wins, and the folders are named in what the person is told
